title: Florida House, District 69
what_it_does: Represents District 69 (Part of Hillsborough) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Daniel Alvarez
candidates.occupation: Attorney (family law) and business consultant; general counsel, Tampa Police Benevolent Association; state representative for District 69 since 2022
candidates.background: Family-law attorney and business consultant who served as an Army infantry officer from 1997 to 2001 and taught business law at the University of Tampa for nearly nine years. He is general counsel for the Tampa Police Benevolent Association and has represented District 69 since 2022, winning re-election in 2024.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F in the June 2026 special session, which placed Amendment 3 on the November ballot to raise the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and to limit how counties and cities may spend property-tax revenue.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (2025), which created the State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state help with federal detainers, barred driver licenses for unauthorized immigrants, and funded an Unauthorized Alien Transport Program.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30

abortion.summary: Voted yes on SB 300 (2023), the law that limits most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 300 (Heartbeat Protection Act, six-week abortion limit), passage 70-40

guns.summary: Voted yes on HB 543 (2023), which allows carrying a concealed firearm without a state license.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HB 543 (concealed carry without a license), passage 76-32

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which removed income limits and enrollment caps so state scholarship funds can follow any K-12 student to private or home education.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (universal school-choice scholarships), passage 83-27

crime.summary: Alvarez says that if re-elected he would build on the public safety legislation he has worked on and continue to support law enforcement and first responders.

healthcare.summary: Alvarez said Florida should focus health spending on the most vulnerable and that he does not believe Medicaid should be expanded to working-aged, able-bodied adults at the expense of other groups.
healthcare.quote: I don't believe we should expand it to work-aged, able-bodied adults at the expense of other groups.

growth.summary: Alvarez named protecting Florida land from rampant overdevelopment that adds traffic and congestion one of his three priorities, and said decisions about data centers should be made at the local level.
growth.quote: Protect our pristine, untouched Florida land from rampant overdevelopment that adds traffic and congestion to our roads.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

insurance.summary: Alvarez said Florida has to keep adjusting its insurance market so insurers are not padding profits and pass savings on, while maintaining a legal climate that brings carriers to the market.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

energy.summary: Alvarez said utilities need to be properly regulated to keep costs low.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

housing.summary: Voted for CS/SB 102 (2023), the 2023 Live Local Act that put $711 million into state housing programs, required local governments to allow multifamily housing in commercial areas when at least 40 percent of units are affordable, and created property-tax exemptions for affordable developments; a vote for it is coded as leaning toward more government action on housing.

elections.summary: Voted for SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.

other_issues.summary: In Sept. 25, 2026 coverage of the District 69 race, Alvarez said protecting the Plant City-area strawberry industry is a priority, describing it as a billion-dollar industry, and listed insurance accountability and conservation among his legislative focuses.

candidates.name: Ashley Herrmann
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Lifelong Floridian, community organizer and self-described democratic socialist who is a first-generation college graduate and mother of two. She has worked at FDOT and in schools, and ran for House District 49 in 2024.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

abortion.summary: She would repeal the six-week abortion law and write a right to abortion into Florida statute.
abortion.quote: Abortion Is Healthcare, Full Stop: Repeal the six-week abortion ban and write the right to abortion straight into Florida law.

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - Healthcare

healthcare.summary: She would expand Medicaid by statute and create a state bridge fund for the ACA subsidy cliff.
healthcare.quote: Expand Medicaid by statute (no constitutional amendment required); create a state bridge fund for the ACA subsidy cliff.

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - Healthcare

housing.summary: She would repeal state bans on local rent caps and short-term rental rules, guarantee lawyers in eviction court and fully fund the affordable housing trust fund.
housing.quote: Repeal the state bans that keep our own city from capping rent hikes or reining in Airbnb.

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - Housing

lgbtq.summary: She would repeal SB 254 (gender-affirming care restrictions), the K-12 classroom restrictions on sexual orientation and gender identity, and HB 1521 (bathroom law), and pass a statewide LGBTQ+ anti-discrimination law.

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - LGBTQ+

immigration.summary: She would repeal the state mandate that local police enter ICE agreements and ban such agreements outright.
immigration.quote: Repeal the state mandate forcing local police into ICE agreements and ban them outright.

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - Safety

crime.summary: She would end private prison contracts and create civilian oversight committees with a public vote before police acquire military gear.
crime.quote: End Florida's private prison contracts and stop rewarding companies like GEO Group.

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - Safety

elections.summary: She would repeal the fines-and-fees requirement for returning citizens to vote, undo barriers to ballot initiatives and restore a simple majority for amendments.
elections.quote: end the pay-to-vote requirement for past convictions

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - Democracy

environment.summary: She would repeal SB 180 to allow stronger post-storm rebuilding rules, stop weakening of wetlands protection, fight offshore drilling and fund Everglades land purchases.
environment.quote: Stop Reckless Development: Repeal the law blocking stronger rebuilding rules after a hurricane and stop the state from weakening wetlands protections.

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - Environment & Climate

energy.summary: She would lock rooftop-solar net-metering rates into statute.
energy.quote: Lock in rooftop solar rates so families who go solar keep what they were promised.

sources.title: Ashley Herrmann for Florida House - Environment & Climate

growth.summary: Herrmann said she would repeal HB 399 so counties can set their own development standards and SB 180 so counties can enforce stronger post-storm rebuilding rules, and would require a binding community benefit agreement before any data center is considered, with a full ban until then.
growth.quote: Require a binding community benefit agreement before any data center is even considered... Until then, full ban, no exemptions.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

property_tax.summary: Herrmann says she opposes Amendment 3, the November 2026 ballot measure that would increase the homestead exemption and reduce property taxes, because of what it would do to local government revenue.
property_tax.quote: I really hope Amendment 3 does not pass

sources.title: DSA-endorsed Ashley Herrmann looks to unseat Hillsborough state Rep. Danny Alvarez

other_issues.title: Says she would push to expand Medicaid and close for-profit prisons
other_issues.summary: In a Sept. 25, 2026 interview, Herrmann said she has looked at expanding Medicaid or using federal dollars Florida has refused in order to bring down health costs. Coverage of the race also reports she supports higher teacher pay, insurance changes and closing for-profit prisons.

sources.title: DSA-endorsed Ashley Herrmann looks to unseat Hillsborough state Rep. Danny Alvarez
Herrmann Challenges Rep. Alvarez in Hillsborough District 69 Race

other_issues.title: Repealing state preemptions of local rules
other_issues.summary: Herrmann said she would repeal Florida's ban on rent control and its short-term-rental, heat-protection and living-wage preemptions, create a wage-theft enforcement unit, cap rental deposits and junk fees, and fund a right-to-counsel pilot for Hillsborough tenants facing eviction.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

other_issues.title: School-entry vaccination rule
other_issues.summary: Herrmann said she would fight to keep science-based school-entry vaccination requirements, criticizing a Florida Department of Health rule she said strips hepatitis B, chickenpox, Hib and pneumococcal vaccines from school-entry requirements.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)
